records.passage: but astronomers note that the supernova is expected to occur within approximately the next 100,000 years and is thus unlikely to be imminent.

records.passage: For various reasons, its distance has been quite difficult to measure; current best estimates are of the order of 400–600 light-years from the Sun – a comparatively wide uncertainty for a relatively nearby star.

narration.text: Betelgeuse will explode, likely within 100,000 years.
It would then shine steadily for 2 to 3 months.
It sits roughly 400 to 600 light-years away.
That's far too distant to harm life on Earth.
In 2019, it dimmed by a factor of about 3.
Many wondered if the explosion had begun. It hadn't.
So the scariest star in Orion is mostly a spectacle.
